title: Sourcegraph Pricing 2026: Plans, Costs and Minimums
summary: Sourcegraph pricing advertises entry costs, but per-seat enterprise fees often run higher. See what each plan actually costs versus the listed price.
body_markdown:
## Sourcegraph Pricing Today, Plan by Plan


### The plans and prices, with check date


Below is each plan I believe is current, with what it includes and the limit that decides whether you fit. I prepared it on 10 November 2026 and couldn't confirm prices against sourcegraph.com/pricing that day, so every price is marked unverified.


Hosted by Sourcegraph and aimed at smaller teams, Enterprise Starter turns on deployment (cloud only) and seat count.


Enterprise is quoted per contract, can be self-hosted or managed, comes with larger scale and admin and security controls, and depends on deployment choice, seat count and usage limits.


Enterprise Starter carries no price I could confirm, so treat it as a per-seat quote you request. Enterprise carries **the $16,000 annual minimum** used throughout this article: that floor applies to Enterprise, and it applies whatever your seat count.


The $16,000 comes from buyer-reported pricing data, not from a figure printed on Sourcegraph's own page, so I'd call my confidence moderate. Confirm it in writing before it goes into a budget.


**The former $49 per user per month rate** was the old per-seat list price. I believe it was retired in 2025, when Sourcegraph moved Enterprise to contract minimums, though I couldn't confirm the exact date.


Amp, Sourcegraph's separate coding agent, is billed on usage rather than seats and sits outside both plans.


### Which limit decides your plan


If your security rules require the code to stay on your own servers, the hosted entry plan is off the table and you're in a quoted conversation. That makes deployment the first limit.


Seat count comes second, because every developer who touches the tool is a seat, including part-timers and contractors.


A team that leans heavily on the AI features can outgrow an allowance that looked generous on paper, because those features are metered. Usage limits come last. Skipping this step is the expensive mistake: you sign for the wrong plan, then pay again to move.


### Plans Sourcegraph has retired or renamed


Old blog posts and comparison pages may quote plans you can no longer buy, because Sourcegraph has reshaped its lineup more than once.


As far as I know, the standalone Cody Free and Cody Pro assistant plans were wound down, and the coding-agent work moved into a separate product.


[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) sits beside Sourcegraph rather than against it, and it meters the run, not the steps inside it: its pricing page lists 1 credit per flow run, however many steps the flow has, so a ten-step flow costs what a two-step one does.
